newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh gang-rape victim returns from India.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh gang-rape victim returns from India.

text.p: A young Bangladeshi girl, smuggled to India and allegedly gang-raped by police, returned home on Thursday after three years protective custody in New Delhi.

The plight of Baby Farida, 14, one of thousands of Bangladeshi girls smuggled to India and Pakistan for prostitution, sparked outrage in India where voluntary groups filed suit in a Delhi court to have the offenders arrested.
Since then four police have been suspended from service, but the cases are still pending in the court.
Farida was likely to stay with the National Women Lawyers Association (BNWLA), which arranged her return, said association executive director Advocate Salma Ali.
"The girl's mother is dead. Her father is a poor farmer and he was not willing to take her back as he has married again," she said.
"This girl was gang-raped by India police," Ali told a news conference.

Traffickers had taken Farida, then aged 10, to Delhi where they were spotted by police, another BNWLA official said. "While the traffickers fled, police got hold of Farida and...took her off the street. Then they gang raped her," she said.
She said Farida was one of thousands of poor Bangladeshi girls smuggled to neighbouring India and other countries for prostitution.
Ali, a leading crusader against trafficking and torture of women, said she had information that some 300,000 Bangladeshi girls worked in brothels in India and another 200,000 in Pakistan.
BWLA had rescued 25 girls from brothels in India's West Bengal state, she said.
Roma Debabrata, an Indian teacher at Delhi University and a social worker, accompanied Farida back to Dhaka.
"I am very happy today that she is back home. I became emotionally attached to the girl over the last three years," Debabrata told the news conference.
"She (Farida) had to suffer a lot at this age," Debabrata said. "She is very depressed. But she is intelligent, affectionate. She sings very good."
